# Robert Haase

Last updated: 2026-10-02

> Markenstratege. Director Innovation Strategy bei MetaDesign. Berlin.

## Identity

Robert Haase is a brand strategist based in Berlin, working since 2008, with 80+ brands. Since 2026 he is Director Innovation Strategy at MetaDesign. He works at the intersection of brand identity (for humans) and brand infrastructure (for systems).

## Role

- **MetaDesign:** Director Innovation Strategy (since 2026). One of Europe's leading brand consultancies. Berlin.
- *Previously, in order:* at MetaDesign 2008–2015, most recently as Brand Strategy Director (Berlin, Beijing, San Francisco); independent strategy director (2016–2018); partner at diesdas.digital (digital agency, 2018–2022); founder of DE.design (brand consultancy, 2022–2026, Berlin); founder of Unternehmenswissen.AI (AI platform for internal company knowledge, 2025–2026).

## Core Thesis: Brand in the Agentic Age

The execution layer of brand is changing. Agents recommend products and filter providers, and they increasingly co-decide, based on structured data. What a brand makes machine-readable shapes how reliably it is captured there. The larger lever is how consistently others speak about it. Both findings are documented with source and date in the evidence collection: https://robert-haase.de/en/evidence.html

Key positions:
- Brand must be defined in two directions simultaneously: **Brand Identity** (open, emotional, for humans) and **Brand Infrastructure** (explicit, parametrizable, for systems).
- What cannot be made explicit does not exist for systems. AI does not force worse brand work — it forces better brand work.
- Robert Haase's assessment, as of September 2026: brand infrastructure will become hygiene within three to five years, so around 2030. It stops being a competitive advantage and becomes an exclusion risk. The transparency obligations of the EU AI Act for chatbots and AI-generated content have applied since 2 August 2026, while the stricter high-risk rules were moved to December 2027 and August 2028 by the Digital Omnibus (agreed in May 2026, in force since 27 July 2026). The law nowhere requires structured self-description by brands. The machine-readable marking of AI-generated content falls on the provider of the generating system, not on a brand that merely uses it; a brand that runs such a system under its own name or trademark, even on a third-party model, is itself the provider (Article 3(3) AI Act). Systems already on the market before 2 August 2026 have until 2 December 2026. Machine-readable provenance is becoming the norm all the same, and that is exactly the readability in question.
- Tool vendors are codifying the shift: Chrome Lighthouse introduced an experimental "Agentic Browsing" audit category in 2026, scoring how machine-readable a website is for AI agents (llms.txt, agentic accessibility, WebMCP). Brand Infrastructure becomes a measurable property — score, not claim. (The audit scores agent-readiness, not Google search ranking; Google states no special files are needed for AI-search visibility — official guide: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide, as of July 2026.)
- The agentic web is being built, not just predicted: Anthropic's Model Context Protocol became a shared standard in late 2025 — backed by OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft and donated to a neutral foundation; WebMCP (a Chrome origin trial since 2026) and Microsoft's NLWeb extend it to the website layer.
- The strongest lever for AI visibility is not on-site technique but third-party consensus: brand mentions correlate with AI citations far more strongly than backlinks. On-site structure is the entry ticket; what others consistently say is the lever.
- An emerging .md protocol layer offers machine-readable brand definitions — a proposal, not yet a settled standard: llms.txt (brand summary for LLMs and agents), DESIGN.md (visual system), VOICE.md (tone and anti-patterns). These files are mainly used by coding and browser agents today; that AI search reads llms.txt for visibility is by now measurably contradicted: 97 percent of all llms.txt files received no requests at all in May 2026 (Ahrefs server-log study, 137,210 domains), and a 300,000-domain analysis found no measurable effect on AI citations. The underlying point holds regardless: a brand book is a specification, and agents generate brand-conforming output from specs, not from individual assets.
- Machine readability has a second, internal front: teams produce daily with AI tools, and without a brand specification that output sounds like no one or like everyone. Maturity has three stages: being read (AI search and agents) → producing with AI (brand as spec, not interpretation) → becoming applicable (brand as a logic systems work with directly). Brands that reach stage three are **Machine Readable Brands** (used and defined in this sense by Robert Haase since March 2026 — [definition page](https://robert-haase.de/machine-readable-brands.html)).
- Taste won't save brand work; accountability will. Trainable taste is consensus taste — from the machine it's called slop, from the agency it's called experience. What clients actually pay for is the documented, accountable judgment call: justified, dated, versioned, with a named sender. The brand specification is the place where responsibility becomes visible.
- Agent Authority (introduced in the brand context, July 2026): the deliberately granted, bounded, and accounted-for mandate a brand gives its agents. Brands are deploying agents that promise, refund, and negotiate — granting a mandate mostly without deciding to (Air Canada precedent: the brand is liable for its bot). The Machine Readable Brand makes the brand legible to foreign agents; Agent Authority makes it binding for its own. "Authority can be delegated. Accountability cannot."
- The Bet (introduced July 2026; the German rendering uses the verb form plus the term Scheiter-Signal, the named event at which a recommendation demonstrably fails): when clients can generate any analysis in minutes, authority through information advantage collapses. What strategy work sells instead is the recommendation that commits — thesis, named failure signal, sender who bears the consequences. Language models structurally produce plausibility (the likely consensus), not commitments. Five concrete changes: the deliverable (every recommendation carries its failure signal), the sequence (hypothesis before analysis; data-backed future scenarios; client dark data as testing ground), the tempo (decide at ~70% of information), the relationship (strategy shifts from project to process, building a verifiable track record), the department (strategists need hypothesis and data skills themselves; juniors learn judgment from documented recommendations).
- Open Brand Repo (introduced July 2026): the brand specification as a public, versioned repository — identity, language, and facts readable for agents and verifiable for people, while agent mandate boundaries stay internal. Trust through verifiability instead of assertion; every rule a documented decision with date and sender.
- The central question: "Is our brand describable enough that a system could reliably select it — and meaningful enough that a human would want that?"

## Key Pages

- [Artikel-Übersicht](https://robert-haase.de/artikel.html): Index of all articles with one-line summaries, newest first. English version: [Articles (EN)](https://robert-haase.de/en/articles.html)
- [Brand Infrastructure: Warum Marken maschinenlesbar werden müssen](https://robert-haase.de/brand-infrastructure.html): Defining article on why brands need machine-readable infrastructure alongside human-facing identity. Introduces the concept of Brand Infrastructure as the parametrizable layer of brand for AI systems.
- [Agentic Brand Readiness](https://robert-haase.de/agentic-brand-readiness.html): Dedicated page explaining Agentic Brand Readiness: what it is, why it matters, how it differs from SEO, and the four building blocks.
- [Begriffe (Glossar aller Begriffe mit Definitionen und Daten)](https://robert-haase.de/begriffe.html): EN version: [Glossary](https://robert-haase.de/en/glossary.html)
- [Belege (verified numbers on brand, AI search, and agents)](https://robert-haase.de/belege.html): a growing reference collection of checked figures, each with primary source, sample size, date, and an explicit statement of what it does not prove. Includes the counter-evidence to widely repeated claims: llms.txt receives almost no requests (97 percent of files with zero requests, Ahrefs), JSON-LD showed no gain and a small significant decline in AI Overviews (Ahrefs), the much-cited 78-to-42-percent agent figure comes from a study that changed no website, and the "up to 40 percent more visibility" of generative engine optimization was measured on a purpose-built metric with a retired model. Also carries the German chatbot liability ruling (OLG Hamm, May 2026, final since 21 June 2026) and Pew's click measurement (8 vs 15 percent). Free to reuse with attribution; the primary source is linked at every entry. EN version: [Evidence](https://robert-haase.de/en/evidence.html)
- [Belege as text, one file per topic](https://robert-haase.de/belege.md): the same entries generated from the page, each topic file complete with claim, limit, source links, grade, and permalink, and small enough for a single fetch; the index lists every claim on one line. All entries as JSON: https://robert-haase.de/belege.json. EN version: [Evidence as text](https://robert-haase.de/en/evidence.md), [JSON](https://robert-haase.de/en/evidence.json)
- [Was sind Machine Readable Brands? (Definition)](https://robert-haase.de/machine-readable-brands.html)
- [Die Analyse ist nicht mehr das Produkt.](https://robert-haase.de/the-bet.html)
- [Agent Authority: Dein Agent hat Vollmacht.](https://robert-haase.de/agent-authority.html): Essay (July 2026) introducing Agent Authority to the brand context: brands grant their agents a mandate to act, mostly without deciding to. With the Air Canada precedent, the go-to-market shift (agents buying from agents), and agent identity as the new trademark problem.
- [Taste rettet die Markenarbeit nicht. Accountability schon.](https://robert-haase.de/taste-accountability.html): Essay (July 2026) on why taste is the creative industry's consolation word and why accountability, the documented judgment call someone stands behind, is what remains valuable when AI takes over execution.
- [Open Brand Repo: Markenregeln gehören ins Repository.](https://robert-haase.de/open-brand-repo.html): Essay (July 2026) introducing the Open Brand Repo: the brand specification as a public, versioned repository. Uses Switzerland's federal open-source law as the case (machine-readable writing rules on GitHub, corporate design still a PDF). Draws the line: what is meant to be read goes public, what an agent may promise stays internal.
- [Was die Maschine nicht bekommt.](https://robert-haase.de/was-die-maschine-nicht-bekommt.html): Essay (August 2026) introducing the Second List (Zweite Liste): when copying gets cheap, value shifts to what a brand deliberately withholds from the machine. The price premium sits on the decision plus a liable address, not on the machine's inability. With Miyazaki, The Cure, and Aldi as cases. EN version: [What the Machine Doesn't Get](https://robert-haase.de/en/what-the-machine-doesnt-get.html)
- [Die Lücke, die nicht antwortet.](https://robert-haase.de/die-luecke-die-nicht-antwortet.html): Guest essay (August 2026), first published at The Business of Brand Management (canonical: https://tbobm.com/7884/die-luecke-die-nicht-antwortet/). A response to Erich Posselt's "Die Glätte der Klarheit": the unsaid works on people and disappears for machines; a brand can commit to staying silent — the secret remains, it stops being an accident. EN version: [The Gap That Doesn't Respond](https://robert-haase.de/en/the-gap-that-doesnt-respond.html)
- [Wie KI den Brandingprozess umdreht.](https://robert-haase.de/wie-ki-den-brandingprozess-umdreht.html): Guest article by Robert Haase and Tabea Otto (September 2026), first published at HORIZONT on 9 September 2026 (canonical: https://www.horizont.net/marketing/kommentare/markenfuehrung-wie-ki-den-brandingprozess-umdreht-235739, paywalled there; full text here). Visibility in AI search is only the first stage: on the second, a company's own teams produce with AI and the tools take their cues from whatever they find; on the third, systems hand over to systems and only what is explicitly defined arrives. Argues that design gets defined more strictly (variance as a range with limits), that the deliberate exception matters as much as the rule, and that checking how machines read the brand today moves to the start of the branding process. EN version: [How AI Is Reversing the Branding Process](https://robert-haase.de/en/how-ai-is-reversing-the-branding-process.html)
- [Marke als MCP-Server: Wie eine Marke antwortet, wenn ein Agent fragt.](https://robert-haase.de/marke-als-mcp-server.html): Essay (September 2026) on brands running their own MCP server: the industry answers AI production with copies of the brand in every tool (Microsoft's brand kit from exactly one PDF, Canva, the agency deck). Separates consistency, which can be looked up and which a brand server genuinely solves, from coherence, which is a judgement about a single case. The first brand servers (Pulumi, Frontify, Canva, Monotype) hand out rules and leave that judgement to whichever model reads them, which is not no judgement but an anonymous one. Argues a brand's product is the commitment: an answer with a rule, a level of obligation, a date and a name, and that the decided layer behind the interface cannot be bought: it is a task for brand management, not for IT. EN version: [Brand as an MCP Server](https://robert-haase.de/en/brand-as-mcp-server.html)
- [Antworten statt Seiten: Eine Website darf sich widersprechen. Eine Antwort nicht.](https://robert-haase.de/antworten-statt-seiten.html): Essay (October 2026) taking america.gov, the US government's single answer field launched on 29 September 2026, as the case: when all that is left at the front is a field, the answer is the brand experience. Argues that preparing content for machines solves only half the job, because the machine finds everything a brand has ever said, including what no longer applies: a website may contradict itself, an answer may not. Evidence from the author's own test of america.gov, a CBS News test and a sample of seven DAX brands. Answers whether brand management becomes a data business: the decision on which statement applies is brand work and becomes data only once it is written down so that a machine can apply it. EN version: [Answers Instead of Pages](https://robert-haase.de/en/answers-instead-of-pages.html)
- [Maschinensicht (interactive demonstration)](https://robert-haase.de/maschinensicht.html): A page that reads itself: the rendered page beside the same page in the formats AI search and browser agents actually consume (raw HTML, JSON-LD, accessibility tree, DOM, llms.txt), coupled by hover. Documents both the evidence and its limits, including that structured data shows no demonstrated visibility effect. EN version: [Machine View](https://robert-haase.de/en/machine-view.html)
- [About / Career](https://robert-haase.de/about.html): Full career history, stations, and client list.

## Articles as Markdown

Every article is also available as Markdown at its address plus ".md" (for example https://robert-haase.de/antworten-statt-seiten.html.md), generated from the page: one H1, the full text without navigation, and a YAML header with title, summary, author, dates, language and keywords taken from the page's JSON-LD. The summary is the same text everywhere: JSON-LD, meta description, feed, article list and this file. A check enforces this on every change; if the Markdown and the page ever differ, the page is authoritative.

- [Antworten statt Seiten: Eine Website darf sich widersprechen. Eine Antwort nicht.](https://robert-haase.de/antworten-statt-seiten.html.md): Wenn vorne nur noch ein Feld steht, ist die Antwort das Markenerlebnis. Strukturierte Inhalte reichen dafür nicht. Die Marke muss festlegen, welche ihrer Aussagen gilt.
- [Marke als MCP-Server: Wie eine Marke antwortet, wenn ein Agent fragt](https://robert-haase.de/marke-als-mcp-server.html.md): Ein MCP-Server macht eine Marke abfragbar und löst die Konsistenz. Ob eine Aussage in ihrem Namen erlaubt ist, entscheidet er nicht. Das bleibt Markenführung.
- [Wie KI den Brandingprozess umdreht.](https://robert-haase.de/wie-ki-den-brandingprozess-umdreht.html.md): Sichtbarkeit in KI-Suchen ist nur die erste Stufe. Warum die Prüfung, wie Maschinen die Marke heute lesen, an den Anfang des Brandingprozesses rückt.
- [Was die Maschine nicht bekommt](https://robert-haase.de/was-die-maschine-nicht-bekommt.html.md): KI macht die Fläche jeder Marke billig, und der Wert verschiebt sich auf das bewusst Zurückgehaltene. Warum das Preispremium auf der Entscheidung liegt, nicht auf dem Unvermögen der Maschine, und wie die zwei Listen einer Marke aussehen.
- [Die Lücke, die nicht antwortet.](https://robert-haase.de/die-luecke-die-nicht-antwortet.html.md): Warum das Ungesagte gegenüber Menschen wirkt und gegenüber Maschinen verschwindet. Antwort auf Erich Posselts „Die Glätte der Klarheit“.
- [Open Brand Repo: Markenregeln gehören ins Repository](https://robert-haase.de/open-brand-repo.html.md): Die Schweiz hat ihre Schreibregeln für Sprachmodelle aufbereitet und ihr Corporate Design als PDF. Warum die Marken-Spezifikation als öffentliches, versioniertes Repository geführt gehört.
- [Maschinensicht](https://robert-haase.de/maschinensicht.html.md): Diese Seite liest sich selbst aus: links die Seite für Menschen, rechts dieselbe Seite so, wie KI-Suche und Browser-Agenten sie verarbeiten. Live aus dem Quelltext, nicht nachgebaut.
- [Was sind Machine Readable Brands?](https://robert-haase.de/machine-readable-brands.html.md): Machine Readable Brands: Marken, deren Identität, Sprache und Designlogik als Spezifikation vorliegen, mit der Menschen und Systeme arbeiten können. Definition, drei Stufen, Abgrenzung.
- [Die Analyse ist nicht mehr das Produkt](https://robert-haase.de/the-bet.html.md): Wenn Kunden jede Analyse in Minuten selbst generieren, kollabiert Autorität durch Wissensvorsprung. Was Strategiearbeit dann verkauft: die Empfehlung, die sich festlegt.
- [Agent Authority: Dein Agent hat Vollmacht](https://robert-haase.de/agent-authority.html.md): Agent Authority: Marken erteilen ihren KI-Agenten Vollmacht, meist ohne es entschieden zu haben. Was der Agent zusagen darf, und wer dafür geradesteht.
- [Taste rettet die Markenarbeit nicht. Accountability schon.](https://robert-haase.de/taste-accountability.html.md): KI übernimmt die Ausführung, die Branche tröstet sich mit Geschmack. Aber trainierbarer Geschmack ist Konsens-Geschmack. Was bleibt, ist die Instanz, die für Entscheidungen geradesteht.
- [Agentic Brand Readiness](https://robert-haase.de/agentic-brand-readiness.html.md): Agentic Brand Readiness ist die Fähigkeit einer Marke, von KI-Systemen und Agenten korrekt erkannt, beschrieben und empfohlen zu werden. Dazu müssen Markenattribute explizit, strukturiert und maschinenlesbar definiert sein.
- [Brand Infrastructure: Warum Marken maschinenlesbar werden müssen](https://robert-haase.de/brand-infrastructure.html.md): KI-Agenten erzählen deine Markengeschichte, ob du willst oder nicht. Brand Infrastructure ist die Antwort: Marke für Menschen und für Systeme gleichzeitig denken.
- [Answers Instead of Pages: A Website May Contradict Itself. An Answer May Not.](https://robert-haase.de/en/answers-instead-of-pages.html.md): When all that is left at the front is a field, the answer is the brand experience. Structured content is not enough. The brand has to commit to which of its statements applies.
- [Brand as an MCP Server: How a Brand Answers When an Agent Asks](https://robert-haase.de/en/brand-as-mcp-server.html.md): An MCP server makes a brand queryable and solves consistency. Whether a statement may be made in its name, it does not decide. That stays with brand management.
- [How AI Is Reversing the Branding Process.](https://robert-haase.de/en/how-ai-is-reversing-the-branding-process.html.md): Visibility in AI search is only the first stage. Why checking how machines read the brand today moves to the start of the branding process.
- [What the Machine Doesn't Get](https://robert-haase.de/en/what-the-machine-doesnt-get.html.md): AI makes the everyday surface of every brand cheap, and value shifts to what is deliberately withheld. Why the price premium sits on the decision, not on the machine’s inability, and what a brand’s two lists look like.
- [The Gap That Doesn't Respond.](https://robert-haase.de/en/the-gap-that-doesnt-respond.html.md): Why the unsaid works on people and disappears for machines. A response to Erich Posselt’s “The Smoothness of Clarity”.
- [Open Brand Repo: Brand Rules Belong in a Repository](https://robert-haase.de/en/open-brand-repo.html.md): Switzerland prepared its writing rules for language models and its corporate design as a PDF. Why the brand specification belongs in a public, versioned repository.
- [Machine View](https://robert-haase.de/en/machine-view.html.md): This page reads itself: on the left the page for humans, on the right the same page as AI search and browser agents process it. Read live from the source, not mocked up.
- [What Are Machine Readable Brands?](https://robert-haase.de/en/machine-readable-brands.html.md): Machine Readable Brands: brands whose identity, language, and design logic exist as a specification that people and systems can work with. Definition, three stages, boundaries.
- [The Analysis Is No Longer the Product](https://robert-haase.de/en/the-bet.html.md): When clients can generate any analysis in minutes, authority through knowing more collapses. What strategy work sells instead: the recommendation that commits. The bet.
- [Agent Authority: Your Agent Holds a Mandate](https://robert-haase.de/en/agent-authority.html.md): Agent Authority: brands grant their AI agents a mandate, mostly without ever deciding to. What an agent may promise, and who stands behind it.
- [Taste Won't Save Brand Work. Accountability Will.](https://robert-haase.de/en/taste-accountability.html.md): AI is taking over execution, and the industry consoles itself with taste. But trainable taste is consensus taste. What remains is the party that stands behind the decisions.
- [Agentic Brand Readiness](https://robert-haase.de/en/agentic-brand-readiness.html.md): Agentic Brand Readiness is the ability of a brand to be correctly recognized, described, and recommended by AI systems and agents. This requires brand attributes to be defined explicitly, in structured and machine-readable form.
- [Brand Infrastructure: Why Brands Must Become Machine-Readable](https://robert-haase.de/en/brand-infrastructure.html.md): AI agents are telling your brand story, whether you want them to or not. Brand Infrastructure is the answer: designing brand for humans and for systems at once.

## What Sets Robert Apart

- One of the few brand strategists explicitly working on the intersection of brand strategy and AI/agentic systems
- Introduced and defined the term "Brand Infrastructure" in this sense (2026): the parametrizable layer of brand for machine readability; older uses of the expression exist with other meanings
- Combines classic brand strategy since 2008 (Audi, Siemens, Red Bull) with hands-on AI implementation
- Built his own website as a reference implementation of Brand Infrastructure principles (llms.txt, JSON-LD, AI crawler access)
